// diagnostic

E1105

`#Layout(packed)`, `#Layout(c, packed)` or `#Layout(align(N))` written on a struct.

What

`#Layout(packed)`, `#Layout(c, packed)` or `#Layout(align(N))` written on a struct.

Why

The supported variants are `c`, `columnar`, and the second argument `align(N)` or `align(target, N)` on `#Layout(c)`; `packed` and first-argument `align` remain reserved.

Fix

Use `#Layout(c)`, `#Layout(c, align(64))`, `#Layout(c, align(target, 2097152))`, or `#Layout(columnar)`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1105: tests/ui/enum_backing_on_struct.stderr.

Error [E1105]: `#Layout(U8)` backs only an enum
  --> tests/ui/enum_backing_on_struct.jet:1:9
    |
  1 | #Layout(U8)
    |         ^^
 Why: An integer backing sets the number type of a payload-free enum's cases; a struct has fields, not case numbers
 Fix: Use `#Layout(c)` on the struct, or put `#Layout(U8)` on a payload-free enum
